newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police close two Islamist offices in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Police close two Islamist offices in Israel.

text.p: Israel closed two offices of an Islamic charity on Monday, alleging they helped "terrorist organisations" by caring for the families of slain members of the militant Hamas group.

Police said that under an order signed by the Israeli army's northern commander, they shut down offices of the Islamic Salvation Committee (ISC) in Nazareth and Umm el-Fahm. Both Arab towns are inside the Jewish state.
"We suspect they helped terrorist groups by caring for the families and children of Hamas people," Avi Tiller, northern district police chief, told Army Radio.
Israel began investigating the group in March following a spate of suicide bombings in Israel in which 59 people were killed.
ISC officials say the charity helps about 10,000 orphans in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza Strip, caring for children regardless of the political affiliations of their parents.
Among aid recipients are about 350 children of suspected Arab informers who were killed by fellow Arabs for helping Israeli security authorities, the officials said.
